implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.__init__ creates paddle_left with up_key=pygame.K_w, down_key=pygame.K_s and paddle_right with up_key=pygame.K_UP, down_key=pygame.K_DOWN

implemented_requirements.requirement: Vertical paddles that move up and down
implemented_requirements.evidence: Paddle.update(keys) changes self.y by self.speed when the assigned up/down keys are pressed and clamps the position within the screen

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball bounces off top and bottom edges
implemented_requirements.evidence: Ball.update() checks self.pos_y <= 0 and self.pos_y + self.size >= settings.SCREEN_HEIGHT and reverses self.speed_y accordingly
Game.check_paddle_collisions() detects rect collisions and calls Ball.bounce_off_paddle(paddle) which reverses horizontal direction and adjusts speed

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players score a point when the opponent misses the ball
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.check_scoring() tests ball.rect.right <= 0 or ball.rect.left >= SCREEN_WIDTH and calls Scoreboard.score_point('right'/'left')
settings.WINNING_SCORE = 5 and Scoreboard.has_winner() returns True when either score reaches this value

implemented_requirements.requirement: Reset the ball after each point
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.after_point() calls self.ball.reset(direction=serve_direction) unless a winner is detected

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game‑over handling and ability to restart
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.game_over flag, Scoreboard.draw_winner(), and Game.restart() which resets scores and ball

judge.summary: All core Pong features are present in the provided source files: two controllable paddles, ball physics with edge and paddle bounces, scoring, a configurable winning score, ball reset after each point, and game‑over/restart logic. The code appears syntactically correct and, assuming pygame can be installed, should run as a functional two‑player Pong game.
